grounding.excerpt_span: During the period beginning the effective date of the permit and lasting through the expiration date of the permit (unless otherwise noted), the permittee is authorized to discharge treated municipal wastewater ... from Outfall 001. Such discharges shall be limited and monitored by the permittee as specified below:
*6      Total dissolved solids measured at Outfall 001. Report the geometric mean value of weekly values.

payload.rationale: The obligation asks whether the 1/Week 12-Hour Composite monitoring for Total Dissolved Solids, Discharge (*6) at Outfall 001 applies only when effluent is discharged from Outfall 001 or throughout the permit term regardless of discharge occurrence. ACCEPT would require establishing one of these readings; REJECT would require establishing that the other reading cannot hold. The packet does not meet either burden. Section A authorizes discharge from Outfall 001 for the full permit term and states that "Such discharges shall be limited and monitored ... as specified below," which links monitoring to authorized discharges but does not unambiguously establish whether monitoring is excused during no-discharge periods or instead continues on the stated calendar frequency for the permit term. Footnote *6 fixes measurement location (Outfall 001) and reporting method (geometric mean of weekly values) but is silent on discharge-conditioned applicability. The parameter label "Discharge" distinguishes this row from the separate intake TDS row but does not by itself establish temporal applicability. Unlike footnote *5 (chlorine use), the TDS Discharge row and footnote *6 contain no explicit "only when discharging" or equivalent temporal condition, so the packet also does not establish permit-term monitoring regardless of flow. With only these excerpts and the packet's own evidence-insufficiency notice, neither discharge-conditioned-only applicability nor permit-term-wide applicability is grounded. Per P5, uncertainty is not converted into semantic closure; UNRESOLVED is the correct disposition.
